y_lines.source: S-02 (spread footing plan) and S-03 (pile footing plan) both print 1.90m from a footing/column row (mark C0, columns 1 and 2 only) up to named grid E -- 2 sheets agree. S-04 (floor-1 beam plan) prints a close but not identical 2.00m at the same position; taken as the same real edge (laundry/utility awning extension) per the 2-sheets-agree rule, with S-04's reading flagged rather than silently discarded.

S-07 (roof frame plan) prints 1.00m eave overhang beyond named grid E, matching the same-size overhang printed on all 4 sides of that sheet, with a real steel eave beam (ตะเข็บลันเหล็ก) drawn at that offset (beam-endpoint rule). S-05 (floor-2 beam plan) prints a close but not identical 1.10m at the same position; taken as the same real roof-eave edge, with S-05's reading flagged rather than silently discarded.

dummy_grid_rule_check.negative_pos_m: 1', E', E'' all sit before the origin (grid 1 / grid E), so all use negative pos_m per §4 rather than taking over the origin position.
dummy_grid_rule_check.prime_ordering: Two dummy lines fall in the same before-origin gap on the y-axis: -1.90 (footing/floor-1 awning) and -1.00 (roof eave). Per §4 'scan in standard reading direction, y-axis top->bottom, first line found = 1 prime', and reading top-to-bottom over this open-ended gap means scanning in increasing-y order starting from far above grid E down toward it -- so the line farther from E (-1.90, encountered first) is E', and the line closer to E (-1.00, encountered second) is E''. This is a genuine judgment call (the rule's worked examples only cover gaps bounded by two named grids), recorded here per §4's 'documenting genuine ambiguity' allowance.

warnings: Main grid (x: 1/2/3 @ 0/5.00/8.50m; y: E/D/C/B/A @ 0/2.70/5.00/8.50/10.00m) is confirmed identically on S-02 (spread footing plan), S-03 (pile footing plan), S-04 (floor 1 beam plan), S-05 (floor 2 beam plan), and S-06 (tie-beam/อะเส plan) — all print the same 8.50 total (5.00+3.50) x-span and 10.00 total (2.70+2.30+3.50+1.50) y-span. Row C's circle label is faint/unclear on S-02 and S-03 (only E/D/B/A circles are legible there) but is clearly printed on A-04 (ground floor architectural plan), which shows all 5 row circles E/D/C/B/A distinctly — used as the confirming source for grid row C. The '10.00' figure printed on S-02/S-03 near the D-to-B gap is the overall check dimension for the full E-to-A span (2.70+2.30+3.50+1.50=10.00), not a separate row gap — resolved by cross-referencing A-04 rather than guessed.

Dummy lines 1'/3'/E'/A' (all at 1.00m beyond the corresponding main grid) are derived from S-07 (roof frame plan), which prints '1.00' overhang dimensions on all four sides beyond the main 1-2-3 x E-A grid, and shows a real steel eave/hip beam (ตะเข็บลันเหล็ก, 2C-125x65x6x8) running along that offset perimeter (beam-endpoint rule, §4) — not merely an architectural roof-overhang annotation. S-04/S-05 (floor beam plans) print a smaller 0.60m dimension in the same header position, but no beam is drawn extending into that 0.60m zone in either floor plan (building outline starts exactly at grid 1/ends exactly at grid 3) — that 0.60 is left unrepresented in the grid master since it never anchors an actual floor beam endpoint; it will be noted per-page if a roof/eave architectural element needs it.
S-06 (อะเส/tie-beam plan) prints its span header as a plain 8.50 with no side margins, confirming the tie-beam ring sits exactly on the main grid with no dummy needed at that level.

z_levels[] built 2026-08-28 by merging the element_type:"level" entries this house's own already-extracted sheets carry (schema section 4: one z_levels[] per building, merged across every sheet that prints levels). Transcription only -- no value was computed and no level was invented; each entry keeps the source_image of the sheet it was read from. Deduplicated on level_m, keeping the printed Thai label and recording any competing label from another sheet in confidence_flags. An installation-height schedule (fixture mounting heights) is deliberately NOT a source -- those are not building levels. dimension_chains[]/unassigned_dimensions[] are still un-swept for this house.
Master was fully unswept before this run (empty dimension_chains[]/unassigned_dimensions[]) -- houses 01-19 class per op_fix skill doc.

NEW x-axis dummy @-1.0 (1.00m before grid 1) and @9.5 (1.00m after grid 3): printed as a roof-eave overhang on S-07 (roof frame plan, หน้า36) and independently confirmed on A-06 roof plan (หน้า08) and all four elevations (หน้า09/11 show it on the x-axis) -- 3 independent sheets agree. Neither position matches an existing line (1'=-0.6, 3'=9.1, which come from a *different* printed 0.60 offset on S-04/S-05/A-04/A-05 beam/floor plans -- the two offsets are genuinely different real edges, not duplicate readings of one edge). Both new points needed because rule 4 (2026-09-27) now requires a line even for a tick nothing structural uses -- this is exactly the case the master's own pre-existing warning text says was 'left unrepresented in the grid master' before the rule existed.

NEW y-axis dummy @11.6 (3.10m beyond grid B, on the far side from C/D/E, i.e. past A and past the existing A' dummy at 11.0): printed on A-13 (รูปตัด 3, หน้า15) as a single continuous dimension line running [new point]--3.10--B--3.50--C--2.30--D--2.70--E--2.00--[E']. Verified via pixel-level crop of the source image that '3.10' truly starts left of B on a line whose direction (this elevation reads B->C->D->E left-to-right, i.e. decreasing pos_m) puts the new point at B(8.5)+3.10=11.60, beyond even the existing A' dummy (11.0). This is a real, previously-dropped tick (likely the ระเบียง/บันได canopy extension past the building envelope on that side) -- not a misread of an already-known line. Only one sheet (หน้า15) shows it; no second sheet available to cross-check, flagged per the 'genuine ambiguity' allowance even though confidence in the transcription itself (verified by direct pixel measurement) is high.

Two pre-existing, already-documented reading disagreements are carried forward faithfully, not silently corrected: S-04 (หน้า33) prints the E-side y-offset as 2.00, but the position it is tied to (line E'', anchored by S-02/S-03's 1.90) is -1.9m from E, i.e. a 0.10m disagreement; the master's own existing warnings[] text already flags this exact case ('S-04...prints a close but not identical 2.00m...taken as the same real edge...flagged rather than silently discarded'). Same situation for S-05 (หน้า34): prints 1.10 at the position of line E''' (-1.10 -- exact match here, no disagreement) but a SEPARATE existing master warning about a *different* S-05 reading (1.10 vs S-07's 1.00 at line E'''') concerns the roof-eave tick at E''''=-1.0, not this one; both are transcribed as printed. Neither disagreement was invented by this sweep -- both are pre-existing master content this sweep is simply now representing as explicit dimension_chains segments instead of prose only.

Site plan (A-03, หน้า05) two outer totals -- x-axis 13.70m ('ต้องการที่ดินกว้างอย่างน้อย = 13.70 ม.') and y-axis 16.20m (same phrasing, 16.20 ม.) -- are recorded as 'edge'-to-'edge' dimension_chains entries, NOT decomposed into the individual 'A'/'B' property-line setback segments the sheet's own notes describe (A = adjustable, minimum 2m; B = adjustable, minimum 3m, per the sheet's own 'หมายเหตุ' legend). Neither individual setback value is printed as a number anywhere on the sheet -- only the combined total is -- and the sheet explicitly states this site plan is illustrative only for cost estimation ('เป็นเพียงตัวอย่างเพื่อประมาณราคา...ส่วนรายละเอียดของสถานที่จริงให้กำหนดรายละเอียดขณะก่อสร้าง'). Computing an individual A/B value by assuming left-right (or top-bottom) symmetry against the total would be inventing a value not printed on any sheet, which is explicitly forbidden -- so both totals stay as unresolvable 'edge' chains, matching the established convention already used for the same situation in a sibling house's staging file (05บ้าน_เล็ก_2ชั้น_03, x-axis 14.1 total).

Two new z_levels (0.50m at ซักล้าง/laundry pad, 0.20m at ห้องน้ำ/จอดรถ pad) and one new z_levels (3.65m, floor-2 bathroom floor level, a 0.10m step-down below ระดับพื้นชั้น2's 3.75) were found -- all three are printed room-level elevation call-outs (▽ style) repeated across multiple sheets, never previously captured in z_levels[] because the master's own prior z_levels build (documented in its existing warnings[]) only merged sheets carrying the element_type:'level' entries already extracted, not every ▽-labelled room floor call-out. None of the three carries a distinct Thai level-id label (only a room name sits beside the number), so id is left null per spec ('If a level is printed with only a number and no label, use null and let level_m carry it').

unassigned_dimensions[] is a representative sample, not exhaustive, for interior/member-detail numbers (door and wall offsets, fixture positions, stair tread runs, room clear-ceiling heights, interior column-to-column spacing not on the main dimension string) across the 20 swept sheets -- every one of these was individually confirmed NOT to touch any x/y/z grid axis line (rule 4's actual scope: 'Not an axis tick: a dimension inside one element's own detail'), so their omission from an exhaustive catalogue does not risk losing a grid line. This is a deliberate efficiency judgment call for a 106-file/113-image house under the task's 'be efficient' instruction; a future full (non-rule-4) dimension sweep of this house, if ever performed, should still re-walk every sheet for completeness of unassigned_dimensions[] rather than trusting this sample as final.

Electrical/AC plan pages หน้า62-66 (floor2 lighting, floor1/floor2 outlets, floor1/floor2 fan/AC position) were NOT reopened individually.
